name: dtls-f26320b2-blind29-ots
instr:
# pion/dtls: 29 injected faults to find without a test suite

This library lets two programs agree on keys over an unreliable datagram link and then exchange application data privately over it. Nothing about the wire format changed and nothing about the callers changed, yet sessions that used to open now fail outright, traffic that used to flow is dropped, and messages that used to be written out and read back unchanged no longer survive the trip. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits.

Choosing what to allow, before anything is sent, already goes wrong. Asking for a top wire-format version of 1.3 while allowing only older-generation encryption choices should settle the permitted span on the older version, and allowing only newest-generation choices should settle it on the newest; both instead come back with the span untouched. Pairing older-generation encryption choices with a key-agreement group only the newest version can use is accepted rather than refused for leaving no version the two ends share. When an unrecognised encryption choice is named, the refusal handed back does not compare equal to the refusal built for that same identifier, though it does match refusals built for different ones. Picking the shared-secret-only encryption choice that pairs block chaining with the 256-bit digest breaks a link in two independent ways: its key material is prepared at the wrong length, and once prepared it claims it is not ready yet, while claiming it is read
